original_question: Find a formula for the number of domino tilings of a 2n-by-(2n+1) Aztec rectangle after deleting its central square.
target_in_paper: Section 3 ("Dominoes"), Problem 9: "Find a formula for the number of domino tilings of a 2n-by-(2n+1) Aztec rectangle with its central square removed." ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the correct family of regions (2n-by-(2n+1) Aztec rectangles), the correct defect (the central square), and the correct task (an exact counting formula for domino tilings). It also does not drift into the distinct neighboring problem where one removes a square adjacent to the center instead. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))
missing_details: Add the quantifier explicitly: the question is meant for each positive integer n (equivalently, for all n >= 1). ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))

Make clear that the region is the standard a-by-b Aztec rectangle used in the paper; the nearby context specifies that Problem 9 sits inside the case of an a-by-b Aztec rectangle with a and b differing by 1 and the larger of a, b odd. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))

Clarify that the deleted cell is the unique central unit square of that Aztec rectangle. The paper’s setup singles out this square in exactly this parity situation. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))
State the tile set explicitly if the question must be fully stand-alone: dominoes are 1-by-2 or 2-by-1 rectangles. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))

If you want the question to be maximally paper-faithful, note that this is exact enumeration of all tilings of the resulting finite region, not an asymptotic, probabilistic, weighted, or generalized variant. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))

No ambient ring/field, operator, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or "sufficiently large" qualifier is relevant here; the hidden assumptions are purely combinatorial (the meaning of Aztec rectangle, central square, domino tiling, and the quantifier on n). ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))
refined_question: For each integer n >= 1, let R_n be the standard 2n-by-(2n+1) Aztec rectangle. Delete its unique central unit square. Determine an explicit exact formula for the number of tilings of the resulting region by 1-by-2 and 2-by-1 dominoes. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Problem 9 in Section 3, not the later adjacent-square variant: the paper first introduces Aztec rectangles with one square removed to restore black/white balance, then states Problem 9 exactly in the 2n-by-(2n+1) central-square case, and immediately contrasts it with Problem 10 for (2n-1)-by-2n rectangles with a square adjoining the center removed. The only refinements needed are to make the quantifier on n explicit and to unpack the implicit meanings of "Aztec rectangle," "central square," and "domino." The paper also records, in the progress note, that this problem had already been solved as a special case of Ciucu’s Theorem 4.1, but the official formulation in the paper is still the Problem 9 wording above. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/matchings.pdf))
